content.text: {"architecturalPlan":{"scaleRationale":"The redesigned Calypsonian House is conceived as a substantial but disciplined waterfront residence: a tall, climate-shaded central salon is the primary social volume, with lower guest, dining, service and ocean-loggia structures forming a protected ground-level ensemble. The upper level is reduced to two separated private-suite enclosures rather than the former overlapping owner, guest and retreat floors. The ambition comes from spatial hierarchy, deep roof shelter, stone-and-timber tectonics and a deliberate arrival sequence rather than unsupported claims about cost, value or certification.","arrivalAndCirculation":"Arrival is organized from the north through a shallow limestone gallery and a recessed bronze entrance, then through a second bronze threshold into the double-height salon. Ground-level doors link the salon to the west guest lounge and east dining room. The ocean loggia is a sheltered outdoor room directly beyond the south salon glazing. The upper owner and guest suite slabs are structurally supported by ground-to-floor cores and are separated in plan; stairs and a fully navigable internal circulation system are not represented.","volumeHierarchy":"A 18m-wide, double-height limestone salon is the dominant volume and visual anchor. A lower arrival gallery gives the entrance a clear civic threshold. The west guest lounge, east dining room and northeast kitchen are deliberately lower, subordinate pavilions. Above the salon, compact owner and guest suite enclosures occupy distinct zones and are held below a single high primary roof. The ocean loggia is an outdoor extension rather than another enclosed wing.","relationshipsAndViews":"The principal south elevation is a broad shaded glazed opening toward the retained pool and waterfront. Smaller, more controlled glazed openings articulate the north, west and east elevations. The guest lounge and dining room each connect directly to the central salon through actual door openings, while the kitchen remains adjacent to dining. The upper suites are separated by a circulation gap and internal enclosure walls to avoid the former overlapping retreat arrangement.","roofFacadeAndMaterials":"A high timber flat roof expresses the primary salon and covers both upper private enclosures. Lower timber roofs shelter the gallery, guest lounge, dining/kitchen and ocean loggia. Limestone is used for substantial wall planes, ivory for private-suite partitions, bronze for doors and glazing frames, and timber for soffits, screens and outdoor shading. Deep roof edges, recessed openings and a slatted ocean screen establish tropical shade without representing unverified ventilation, drainage or weather-performance analysis.","intendedSpaces":["North arrival gallery with recessed main entrance","Double-height ocean salon","West guest lounge","East dining room","Northeast kitchen/service room","Sheltered ocean loggia","Separated upper owner suite enclosure","Separated upper guest suite enclosure","Retained pool precinct, not redesigned in this pass"],"designDecisions":[{"disposition":"constructed","knowledgeId":"property-value-25m-50m","decision":"Used the ambition reference to create a clear estate-scale hierarchy: bespoke arrival, dominant shared living volume, protected private suites and sheltered ocean entertaining, without making a value or cost claim.","elementIds":["salon-floor","gallery-floor","salon-roof","ocean-loggia-roof","owner-floor","guest-floor"],"limitation":"No construction-cost, property-value, luxury certification, service or amenity claim is represented."},{"disposition":"constructed","knowledgeId":"facade-materials","decision":"Applied a restrained limestone, ivory, timber and bronze palette with recessed openings, deep roof shelter and a timber ocean screen around the rebuilt residence.","elementIds":["salon-south-wall-new","arrival-north-wall-new","salon-roof","ocean-screen-new","main-entrance-new"],"limitation":"Material selections are editable scene materials only; no specialist finish, weathering or craftsmanship certification is represented."},{"disposition":"constructed","knowledgeId":"roof-main-secondary","decision":"Established a high primary roof over the salon and reduced roofs over arrival, guest, dining, kitchen and loggia volumes.","elementIds":["salon-roof","gallery-roof-new","guest-lounge-roof-new","dining-roof-new","kitchen-roof-new","ocean-loggia-roof"],"limitation":"Roof waterproofing, drainage, loading and guard-code compliance are not represented."}]}, "name":"Calypsonian House — Waterfront Courtyard Redesign","summary":"The inadequate fragmented house is replaced by a coherent limestone-and-timber waterfront composition: a high central salon, north arrival gallery, lower guest/dining/service pavilions, sheltered ocean loggia, and two non-overlapping upper private-suite enclosures. The pool/site elements are preserved. Former elevated terrace decks and their incorrectly positioned rails are removed rather than retained, eliminating the Y=3.8 versus Y=4.2 coordination issue.","unsupported":["The new-generation scene remains on the existing flat Y=0 ground plane; no terrain modification is made.","Stairs, lift, fully navigable upper-level circulation, bathrooms, closets, kitchen equipment, HVAC, drainage and structural engineering are not represented.","The upper suite floors have modeled ground-to-floor support cores, but no engineering certification is implied.","The retained pool geometry is preserved as unrelated site work; it is not re-described as a complete pool system or as a hydraulic infinity edge. Its missing north coping/basin treatment is outside this redesign scope.","Interior furniture, room fit-out, code compliance, fire egress and weather-performance simulation are
